clue.text: Band's jacket recommendation? Not black

indicators.note: 'Not black' tells us to drop the letter standing for black from the recommendation

parts.note: a blurb is the praise printed on a book's jacket
B is the pencil-grading abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A musician asks what jacket to wear on stage, and is told anything but black.
explanation.definitionFit: Blur were a leading Britpop group of the 1990s, so the name fits a band.

clue.text: Hybrid court

definitions.meaning: a mixture made of several parts combined
an enclosed yard or area, as in a prison exercise yard

explanation.definitionFit: Something mixed from elements is a composite; an enclosed courtyard or pen is the other sense.

clue.text: Vehicle carrying Latin duo

indicators.note: a vehicle carrying something holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a coupe is a two-door car

explanation.surface: A car is transporting a pair of Latin speakers or performers.
explanation.definitionFit: A duo is a pair, two people together, which is what this word means.

clue.text: Iris affected with bust and shoulder inflammation

indicators.note: affected suggests something altered or disturbed, so the letters of iris and bust are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone named Iris suffers a painful shoulder along with trouble around the chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' signals rearranging IRIS and BUST together; 'with' merely links them to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is swelling of a bursa, a fluid sac cushioning a joint, commonly in the shoulder.

clue.text: Sing about high priest's balloon content?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the singing word is wrapped around the priest

parts.note: to hum is to sing with closed lips
Eli was the high priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A chorister is told to sing about the high priest's balloon, a curious instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that balloon filling is one example of the gas, not a full definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This light, non-flammable gas is what fills party balloons so they float.

clue.text: Thumb stuck under a basic building block?

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece stuck under another comes after it in the column

parts.note: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of a folk tale

explanation.surface: A thumb is wedged beneath a basic toy brick.
explanation.definitionFit: Matter is built up from these tiny particles, so it is a fundamental unit of construction.

clue.text: Cola formula, almost pure drink

indicators.note: a formula is a recipe or arrangement, so the letters of cola are rearranged
almost means the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: holy means pure or sacred

explanation.surface: A cola recipe is said to be practically a pure, wholesome drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formula' turns COLA into ALCO; 'almost' cuts HOLY to HOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits, beer and wine are collectively called by this word, a general term for drink.

clue.text: Spread butter, with end of knife that's used to deliver liquid

indicators.note: spread suggests the letters are smeared out into a new order
the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Instructions for spreading butter with the tip of a knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' rearranges BUTTER; 'end of' takes the last letter of knife, E.
explanation.definitionFit: This graduated glass tube with a tap dispenses measured volumes of liquid in titrations.

clue.text: See 21 down
'K' is wrestling with Pat (sumo)

indicators.note: wrestling suggests bodies tangled and thrown about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A wrestler called K is grappling with Pat at sumo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrestling' rearranges IS, PAT and SUMO together.
explanation.definitionFit: K is the chemical symbol for this alkali metal, from its Latin name kalium.

clue.text: It's probably not good to eat nasty people with a utensil

definitions.text: It's probably not good to eat

parts.note: toads are loathsome, contemptible people
a tool is an implement or utensil

explanation.surface: A warning that it's bad manners to dine with unpleasant company using some implement.
explanation.definitionFit: Many wild fungi of this kind are poisonous, so eating one is usually unwise.

clue.text: Announced fruit's value

indicators.note: announced means said out loud, so we want a word that sounds like the fruit

parts.note: a gage is a greengage, a kind of plum

explanation.surface: Someone declares what a piece of fruit is worth.
explanation.definitionFit: To value something is to estimate or measure it, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: All right at start of cruise, for example, to go round the Lizard?

indicators.note: going round means turning back, so the assembled string is read in reverse

parts.note: OK means all right

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cruise ship sails round the Lizard, the Cornish headland, and all is well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Lizard' looks like the Cornish peninsula, the most southerly point of mainland Britain; here it is just a reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: This small, often wall-climbing reptile is a type of lizard.

clue.text: One's taken by Mark, perhaps, to be a metalloid

indicators.note: taken by means received into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Mark Antony, the Roman general, so Antony is one example
one's contracts to I'm, which gives I and M

explanation.surface: Someone named Mark accepts a part and becomes a semi-metal.
explanation.definitionFit: This brittle element, symbol Sb, has properties between metals and non-metals.

clue.text: Head appearing on large English coin

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece appearing on others sits above them

parts.note: nob is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A monarch's head appears on a big English coin.
explanation.definitionFit: This was an old English gold coin, first minted under Edward III.

clue.text: Support needed to hold C sharp

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so C goes within the support

parts.note: aid means support or help

explanation.surface: A musician needs support to hold a C sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'C sharp' looks like the musical note, but 'sharp' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp means tart or sour-tasting, as acidic flavours are.

clue.text: Talk drugs, mustard and marsh, say?

parts.note: gas is idle chatter
E is slang for ecstasy, so Es means several of these tablets

explanation.surface: Chat about narcotics, condiments and wetlands, a rambling conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Mustard gas and marsh gas are both examples of airy substances, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Wood to sell back disco?

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to flog is British slang for to sell
a club is a nightclub or disco

explanation.surface: A timber merchant offers to sell wood back to a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood' suggests timber, but it is a golf club with a large head, once made of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, a wood is a long-distance stick with a broad head, the driver being one.

clue.text: See 22
'To the bride', perhaps, in German (Browning)

parts.note: a toast is a raised-glass tribute such as 'to the bride'

explanation.surface: A wedding toast is given in German, with a nod to the poet Browning.
explanation.walkthrough: Browning looks like the poet but is the definition: cooking brown under a grill.
explanation.definitionFit: Browning bread under heat is exactly the cooking process meant here.

clue.text: Fancy doorbell, but not a respectable place

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornamental, so the letters are dressed up in a new order

explanation.surface: An elaborate doorbell, yet the house it belongs to is disreputable.
explanation.definitionFit: A brothel is a disreputable house, and this is another word for one.

clue.text: Chemist and singer residing in the outskirts of Darwin

indicators.note: residing in means living inside, so the singer goes within the outer letters
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice

explanation.surface: A scientist and a vocalist live on the edge of the Australian city of Darwin.
explanation.walkthrough: Darwin looks like the naturalist, but here it only supplies D and N.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dalton was the English scientist who proposed modern atomic theory.

clue.text: Stage broadcast worry

indicators.note: broadcast means put out over the air, so we want the sound of the synonym

parts.note: to faze is to worry or disconcert

explanation.surface: A performer is anxious about a stage show that is being broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage of development is a step or period in a process.

clue.text: Term for each moon day

parts.note: per means for each
Io is one of Jupiter's moons

explanation.surface: A school term arranged with a lesson for each moon day.
explanation.definitionFit: A term is a span of time, such as a school session, which matches this word.

clue.text: Instant cure-all, possibly composed of tiny pieces

parts.note: mo is short for moment, an instant

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible arrangement of the letters of cure-all

explanation.surface: An instant panacea might be broken down into minute fragments.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the smallest units of a substance, made of particles bound together.

clue.text: Plan to acquire curling rink, including wide, controversial shoulder protection

indicators.note: to acquire is to take in, so the plan wraps around the jumble

parts.note: a map is a plan or chart

indicators.note: including means taking something in, so the letter for wide goes inside the rearranged rink
curling means twisting or bending, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: Someone plans to take a curling rink on, while wearing a contentious fur stole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curling' looks like the ice sport at the rink, but it rearranges RINK to INKR; 'including' then puts W inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: A fur stole worn over the shoulders; fur is ethically disputed, hence controversial.

clue.text: River transport laboratory item

parts.note: the Test is a river in Hampshire, England, famous for trout fishing
the Tube is London's underground railway

explanation.surface: A river boat carries some laboratory equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin glass cylinder closed at one end, a standard piece of lab glassware.

clue.text: Was a killer from Isleworth?

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the place name

explanation.surface: Was there a murderer from Isleworth, a district of west London?
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of slay, to kill, so it means killed.

clue.text: Sharp cousin, several times removed, biting head off fellow

indicators.note: biting means holding in the teeth, so one piece is enclosed by the other
a distant cousin is several times removed, which here says the letters are moved around
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A distant relative bites the head off a man in a fit of temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'several times removed' rearranges COUSIN to INOCUS, and 'biting' puts F, the head of fellow, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture that is sharp is clear and properly focused, the idea of this phrase.

clue.text: Titled person on revolving bar

parts.note: a count is a nobleman with a title

indicators.note: revolving means turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A nobleman sits on a rotating bar stool.
explanation.definitionFit: A counter is the long table in a shop or pub across which goods are served, a bar.
